t:
(a) In General.—There are hereby appropriated for fiscal year 2014, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, for any period during which interim or full-year appropriations for fiscal year 2014 are not in effect—
        (1) such sums as are necessary to provide pay and allowances to members of the Armed Forces (as defined in section 101(a)(4) of title 10, United States Code), including reserve components thereof, who perform active service during such period; 
        (2) such sums as are necessary to provide pay and allowances to the civilian personnel of the Department of Defense (and the Department of Homeland Security in the case of the Coast Guard) whom the Secretary concerned determines are providing support to members of the Armed Forces described in paragraph (1); and 
        (3) such sums as are necessary to provide pay and allowances to contractors of the Department of Defense (and the Department of Homeland Security in the case of the Coast Guard) whom the Secretary concerned determines are providing support to members of the Armed Forces described in paragraph (1).  
    (b) Secretary Concerned Defined.—In this section, the term “Secretary concerned” means—
        (1) the Secretary of Defense with respect to matters concerning the Department of Defense; and 
        (2) the Secretary of Homeland Security with respect to matters concerning the Coast Guard.

fable.w: This section only appropriates funds for pay and allowances to service members, civilian personnel, and contractors during a lapse in appropriations. The tempting reading is that the mention of contractors (outside parties) and a determination by the "Secretary concerned" signals outside involvement, but contractors are merely payment recipients and the determination is made unilaterally by a federal official. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with non-federal entities, or right to sue.
fable.s: such sums as are necessary to provide pay and allowances to contractors of the Department of Defense (and the Department of Homeland Security in the case of the Coast Guard) whom the Secretary concerned determines are providing support to members of the Armed Forces

qwen_block.w: This section is an appropriation provision that authorizes the payment of salaries and allowances to federal employees (Armed Forces members, civilian personnel) and contractors. It does not establish any process for outside parties to consult with, advise, or participate in federal decision-making. The mention of contractors refers to the recipients of payment, not participants in a governance or advisory role.
qwen_block.s: such sums as are necessary to provide pay and allowances to members of the Armed Forces... to the civilian personnel of the Department of Defense... and to contractors of the Department of Defense

opus.w: This section only provides money to pay military members, civilian staff and contractors during a lapse in appropriations. Contractors are named only as people who get paid. They are not consulted and play no part in any federal decision. The Secretary of Defense or Homeland Security makes the decisions alone, with no comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue.
opus.s: such sums as are necessary to provide pay and allowances to contractors of the Department of Defense (and the Department of Homeland Security in the case of the Coast Guard) whom the Secretary concerned determines are providing support to members of the Armed Forces

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes appropriations for pay and allowances for military, civilian, and contractor personnel. It does not require the federal government to consult or coordinate with outside parties before making decisions. The determination of who receives pay is an internal administrative function, and the contractors are recipients of compensation, not participants in a policy decision-making process. The definition excludes applications for benefits or grants, and this text is purely about funding authorization.
qwen_chat.s: such sums as are necessary to provide pay and allowances to contractors of the Department of Defense (and the Department of Homeland Security in the case of the Coast Guard) whom the Secretary concerned determines are providing support to members of the Armed Forces described in paragraph (1).
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Secretary determines which contractors or civilian personnel receive pay, this involves a decision-making process that could imply consultation. However, the text only describes the appropriation of funds and the authority to determine eligibility for payment based on support roles. It does not mandate any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties (such as the contractors themselves, the public, or state governments) before making these determinations. The actors involved (Secretary of Defense, Secretary of Homeland Security, military members, civilian personnel, contractors) are either inside the federal government or are recipients of funds/employment, not participants in a policy decision-making process as defined. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and this is essentially an authorization for payment.
